segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. Your current term runs through August 31, so I wanted to walk through the renewal and the seat change before your July budget lock.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yep, good timing. We’re at 42 seats today. Finance approved moving to 55, but they want the invoice to hit after July 15, not before.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Got it. For 55 seats on the business plan, annual term, the pricing sheet has it at $38 per seat per month. That comes to $25,080 for the year, starting September 1 through August 31 next year.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. Is there any implementation fee for adding the 13 people, or is that just admin on our side?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: No implementation fee. We’ll include one 60-minute admin enablement session, and your users can be added any time after the order form is signed. If you want, we can target September 3 for the session.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: September 3 works. One thing, legal asked if the auto-renew language can stay the same as this year, 30-day notice window.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, same contract terms as your current agreement: annual term, net 30, 30-day notice before renewal. No change there.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. Can you show the invoice as one annual line item? Our AP team gets picky if it’s split by department.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, one annual subscription line for 55 seats, $25,080, invoice dated July 16, service period September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. Send it to me and copy Marcus in finance. If it matches what we discussed, I can sign by Friday.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I’ll send the order form today with Marcus copied, and I’ll include the September 3 enablement date in the notes so the handoff is clean.
